requirements.name: NCAGE code
requirements.summary: A five-character entity identifier from the NATO codification system. Needed for NATO and NSPA supply and for stock numbers. Free of charge.
requirements.description:
The NATO Commercial and Government Entity (NCAGE) code is a five-character entity identifier. It is required for NATO Stock Number (NSN) assignment, for registration in NATO and national supply systems, and for procurement through NSPA. Holding an NCAGE code does not give any right to use NATO branding.

Who handles the request depends on the country. For NATO countries and a defined Tier 2 list, the request is handled by the national codification bureau (NCB); for everyone else NSPA handles it directly. The Tier 2 list includes Ukraine, alongside ARE, ARG, AUS, AUT, BRA, COL, GEO, IND, IDN, ISR, JOR, JPN, KOR, MYS, MAR, NZL, SRB, SGP and QAT.

The request starts in the NCAGE request tool: three mandatory fields on the first step (type of entity, other/priority, country), then a validation link is sent to the person who started it. Once validated, the priority cannot be changed.

days.text: Up to 14 working days on average; routine priority is 10 calendar days, emergency is 3 working days
days.note: Working days are converted to calendar days at 7/5 and rounded up: 3 working days is 5 calendar days and 14 working days is 20.

requirements.mandatory_for: NATO and NSPA supply; NATO Stock Number assignment. Not an eligibility condition of EDF, EDIP or SAFE.

passages.ref: NSPA, quoted in the DefenceGate technical appendix, NCAGE
passages.text: In accordance with NATO policy, the assignment and update to the NCAGE are free of charge.

requirements.name: PIC (Participant Identification Code)
requirements.summary: A nine-digit code issued when an organisation registers on the EU Funding and Tenders Portal. Free and immediate. Needed to apply for EDF and EDIP funding.
requirements.description:
Register the organisation on the Funding and Tenders Portal through a six-step wizard. A nine-digit PIC is issued immediately when the wizard is complete. An EU Login account is needed. Incomplete drafts are deleted after one year.

Validation by the Central Validation Service (legal entity form, a recent VAT extract, a registration extract or the statutes) is required only if a proposal is selected for funding; for many grants REA performs it. A Legal Entity Appointed Representative (LEAR) must be appointed to update the organisation's data and to handle electronic signatures. A financial capacity assessment applies to grants, except for public bodies and certain other cases.

days.text: Immediate on completing the registration wizard

requirements.source_ref: EU Funding and Tenders Portal, Participant Register

passages.ref: DefenceGate technical appendix, Participant Register and PIC
passages.text: register the organisation on the Funding and Tenders Portal through a six-step wizard. A nine-digit PIC is issued immediately on completion. EU Login required.

requirements.name: SAFE origin rule (Article 16)
requirements.summary: In a SAFE-supported procurement, components from outside the Union, the EEA EFTA states and Ukraine may not cost more than 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product, and no component may come from a third country that contravenes the Union's security and defence interests.
requirements.description:
The 35 % is measured against the estimated cost of the components of the end product. It is not measured against the contract value; briefings often paraphrase it wrongly as a share of contract value. There is also a separate, absolute prohibition: no component at all may be sourced from a third country that contravenes the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States. The percentage allowance does not cover it.

The same Article also sets rules on establishment, executive management and control for contractors and subcontractors; they are listed on the SAFE card of the readiness page.

passages.text: The cost of components originating outside the Union, EEA EFTA States and Ukraine shall not be higher than 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product. For the purpose of procurements supported by the SAFE instrument, no component shall be sourced from a third country that contravenes the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States.

requirements.name: ISO 9001 quality management certificate
requirements.summary: The general quality management standard. AQAP 2110 contains all of ISO 9001:2015, so holding it makes the AQAP path shorter and cheaper.
requirements.description:
AQAP 2110 contains the whole of ISO 9001:2015 plus NATO-specific additions. In practice: build ISO 9001 first, then add the NATO layer. Companies that already hold ISO 9001 face a materially shorter and cheaper path to AQAP 2110.

The research behind this page has no source for the cost or duration of ISO 9001 itself, so none is shown.
requirements.mandatory_for: Prerequisite of AQAP 2110 in practice. Not an eligibility condition of EDF, EDIP or SAFE.

passages.ref: DefenceGate technical appendix, AQAP and quality certification
passages.text: AQAP 2110 contains the whole of ISO 9001:2015 plus NATO-specific additions: configuration management, risk management, product dependability, and the customer state's right to conduct Government Quality Assurance (GQA) during contract performance.

requirements.name: EN 9100 / AS9100 certificate

requirements.description:
AQAP 2310 contains EN 9100 / AS9100 Rev D plus NATO additions. AQAP does not replace EN 9100: it is a superset.

The research behind this page has no source for the cost or duration of EN 9100 itself, so none is shown.

requirements.name: AQAP 2110 quality assurance certification
requirements.summary: NATO quality assurance requirements for design, development and production. Not an eligibility condition of EDF, EDIP or SAFE: it enters through individual contracts and cascades down the supply chain.
requirements.description:
AQAP 2110 Edition D Version 1 was promulgated by the NATO Standardization Office on 24 June 2016 and is still in force in 2026. AQAP 2210 (software quality requirements) is layered on AQAP 2110 or 2310 and is not standalone. AQAP 2120 no longer exists separately: it was folded into AQAP 2110 when Edition D was issued in 2016, so anyone still asking for AQAP 2120 is working from stale guidance.

Do you need it for EDF? Not to apply, but likely to deliver. No blanket AQAP requirement appears in the EDF, EDIP or SAFE regulations as an eligibility condition (those regulate control, establishment and component origin). It enters when a prime contractor or a national buyer names it in a contract, and it then cascades down to subcontractors.

Issued by national defence authorities (Government Quality Assurance) or by accredited certification bodies, depending on the country. Certificates run for three years with annual surveillance audits.

requirements.name: Export authorisation for dual-use or military items
requirements.summary: An authorisation to export items in a controlled category. Which licence depends on whether the item is in the dual-use regime or the military regime.
requirements.description:
Two regimes are frequently confused. Dual-use items fall under Regulation (EU) 2021/821, whose Annex I is the control list. Military goods fall under the Common Military List, with transfers inside the EU governed by Directive 2009/43/EC and separate licences. A product can be in the military regime and not the dual-use one, so the first question is which regime applies.

The exporter is responsible for deciding whether its product matches an Annex I entry. Customs and tariff codes only signal that control is possible; they do not settle it. The basis is the manufacturer's datasheet and, where uncertain, a formal classification request to the competent authority.

This service asks which regime applies to your product and names the competent authority for the countries where we collected it (Spain, Germany and Poland). It does not tell you whether a given category needs a licence, it does not publish control list parameters or technical thresholds, and it gives no advice on controlled items.
requirements.legal_basis: Regulation (EU) 2021/821; Directive 2009/43/EC; Council Common Position 2008/944/CFSP; in Spain Ley 53/2007 and Real Decreto 679/2014
requirements.mandatory_for: Export of items in controlled categories.

passages.text: An authorisation shall be required for the export of dual-use items listed in Annex I.

requirements.name: HSEM facility security clearance (Spain)
requirements.summary: The Spanish facility security clearance (Habilitación de Seguridad de Empresa), needed to handle classified information. How long it takes is not published.
requirements.description:
In Spain the National Security Authority is the Oficina Nacional de Seguridad (ONS), which works under the Secretaria de Estado Directora del CNI as the delegated authority for the security of classified information of NATO, the EU and ESA. The facility clearance is called HSEM (Habilitación de Seguridad de Empresa); the ONS maps it to the international Facility Security Clearance Information Sheet (FSCIS).

Related clearances: HSES (Habilitación de Seguridad de Establecimiento) is for storing classified material on your own premises and requires HSEM first; HPS (Habilitación Personal de Seguridad) is the individual clearance.

How long an HSEM takes was not published and needs a direct enquiry to the ONS. Other countries have their own National Security Authority; the research behind this page has collected only Spain's.

rules.title: Established in the Union or an associated country

texts.requires: Recipients and subcontractors involved in an action must be established in the Union or in an associated country: an EEA EFTA state, or Ukraine, on the conditions of the agreements that associate them.
texts.met: Your company is established in an EU Member State, an EEA EFTA state or Ukraine. These are the Union and the associated countries of the EDF.
texts.not_met: Your company is established outside the EU, the EEA EFTA states and Ukraine. EDF recipients must be established in the Union or in an associated country.
texts.unknown: Say in which country your company is established.

rules.note: The associated countries are the EEA EFTA states (under the conditions of the EEA Agreement) and, since Regulation (EU) 2025/2653, Ukraine (under the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement).

rules.title: Executive management in the Union or an associated country

texts.requires: Their executive management structures must be established in the Union or in an associated country, and the infrastructure, facilities, assets and resources used for the action must be located there for the whole action.

rules.note: The same paragraph requires that the infrastructure, facilities, assets and resources used for the action are located in a Member State or an associated country for the whole duration of the action. This service does not ask about that.

passages.text: The infrastructure, facilities, assets and resources of the recipients and subcontractors involved in an action which are used for the purposes of an action supported by the Fund shall be located on the territory of a Member State or of an associated country for the entire duration of an action, and their executive management structures shall be established in the Union or in an associated country.

rules.title: Not controlled by a non-associated third country

texts.requires: Recipients and subcontractors must not be subject to control by a non-associated third country or entity, unless guarantees approved by the Member State or associated country where they are established are made available to the Commission.
texts.met: Your company is not controlled from a non-associated third country. Control from an EEA EFTA state or Ukraine does not count against you under the EDF.
texts.not_met: Your company is controlled from a non-associated third country.
texts.conditional: Your company is controlled from a non-associated third country. It can still be eligible, but only if guarantees approved by the Member State or associated country where it is established are made available to the Commission.
texts.unknown: Say whether your company is controlled by a country or an entity outside the EU, the EEA EFTA states and Ukraine. If you do not know, find out who your ultimate owners are.

rules.note: The guarantees must show that control is not exercised in a way that restricts the action, that access to sensitive information is prevented, and that intellectual property stays with the recipient. Paragraph 4 of Article 9 lists them.

passages.text: For the purposes of an action supported by the Fund, the recipients and subcontractors involved in an action shall not be subject to control by a non-associated third country or by a non-associated third-country entity.

By way of derogation from paragraph 3, a legal entity established in the Union or in an associated country and controlled by a non-associated third country or a non-associated third-country entity shall be eligible to be a recipient or subcontractor involved in an action only if guarantees approved by the Member State or the associated country in which it is established in accordance with its national procedures are made available to the Commission.

rules.title: Subcontractors outside the Union: the 15 to 35 % allowance

texts.info: A procurement can include a subcontractor that is allocated between 15 % and 35 % of the value of the contract and is not established, or has no executive management structures, in the Union, an EEA EFTA state or Ukraine, if at least one of two conditions is met: a direct contractual relationship related to the defence product existed between the contractor and that subcontractor before this Regulation entered into force (it was published on 28 May 2025 and entered into force on the following day, 29 May 2025), or the contractor commits to study within two years replacing its input. This figure is a share of the contract value. It is not the 35 % component cost threshold above.

passages.text: By way of derogation from paragraph 3, in order to take into account industrial cooperation with non-EU partners, common procurements that involve a subcontractor which is allocated between 15 % and 35 % of the value of the contract, and that is not established or doesn’t have its executive management structures in the Union, EEA EFTA State or Ukraine, shall be eligible for support under the SAFE instrument providing that at least one of the following conditions are met:
a direct contractual relationship related to the defence product has been established between the contractor and that subcontractor prior to the date of entry into force of this Regulation;

the contractor commits to studying, within two years, the feasibility of replacing the input provided by that subcontractor with an alternative, restriction-free input originating in the Union, EEA EFTA States or Ukraine, and meeting technical and time requirements.

rules.title: Legal entity: a legal person, not a natural person

texts.requires: A recipient must be a legal entity: a legal person, or an entity without legal personality that meets the conditions the Financial Regulation sets for such entities.
texts.met: Your organisation is a legal person, which the regulation counts as a legal entity.
texts.not_met: A natural person, for example a sole trader acting in their own name, is not a legal entity as this regulation defines it. The definition names legal persons and, from the Financial Regulation, only entities without legal personality (point (c)). Natural persons are a separate category of the Financial Regulation (point (b)), which the definition does not cite. Take part through a legal person, or ask the contact point of the call whether your case is accepted.
texts.conditional: Your organisation has no legal personality. It counts as a legal entity only if it is an entity of the kind described in Article 197(2), point (c), of the Financial Regulation: its representatives can undertake legal obligations on its behalf and it offers guarantees for the protection of the Union's financial interests equivalent to those of a legal person. The Commission assesses that in the call.
texts.unknown: Say what legal form your organisation has: a legal person (for example a company), a natural person (for example a sole trader), or an entity without legal personality.

rules.note: Whether a particular national form, such as a sole trader or a partnership, falls on one side or the other is not settled by the regulation's words alone; the call and the Commission decide. This service reads only the definition.
rules.source_ref: Regulation (EU) 2021/697, Article 2 (definition of 'legal entity') and Article 9(1)

passages.text: ‘legal entity’ means a legal person created and recognised as such under Union, national or international law, which has legal personality and the capacity to act in its own name, exercise rights and be subject to obligations, or an entity which does not have legal personality as referred to in point (c) of Article 197(2) of the Financial Regulation;

passages.ref: Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2018/1046 (the Financial Regulation that Regulation 2021/697 cites), Article 197(2)
passages.text: 2. rules.title: Components from outside the Union and associated countries: at most 35 % of component cost

texts.requires: In procurement and industrial reinforcement under the Programme, the cost of components originating outside the Union and associated countries may be at most 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product.
texts.met: The share of components from outside the Union, the EEA EFTA states and Ukraine is within 35 %, and you report no component from Ukraine or an EEA EFTA state. Under the Programme the limit is 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product.
texts.conditional: Your share of components from outside the Union, the EEA EFTA states and Ukraine is within 35 %, but some components come from Ukraine or an EEA EFTA state. Under the Programme, Ukraine is not an associated country, so components from Ukraine count as coming from outside the Union and the associated countries: add their share to your figure, and the total may not exceed 35 %. Components from an EEA EFTA state count as inside only if that state applies the Regulation.
texts.not_met: More than 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product comes from outside the Union, the EEA EFTA states and Ukraine. Under the Programme the limit is 35 % for components from outside the Union and the associated countries, and components from Ukraine count against it as well.
texts.unknown: Give the share of the estimated cost of the components of your end product that originates outside the Union, the EEA EFTA states and Ukraine, and say whether any component originates in Ukraine or in an EEA EFTA state.

rules.note: Article 10(3) applies to procurement under Articles 11, 13 and 35. For industrial reinforcement actions (Article 12) paragraph 4 sets the same limit, measured on the product whose production capacity the funding supports. Paragraph 5 also requires that recipients can decide on the design of the products without restrictions imposed by non-associated third countries; this service does not ask about that. The answer is about one end product.

rules.denominator: the estimated cost of the components of the end product (for industrial reinforcement actions, of the product whose production capacity the funding supports)

passages.text: For procurement carried out pursuant to Articles 11, 13 and 35 which is supported by Union funding, the cost of components originating outside the Union and associated countries shall not be higher than 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product.

For actions carried out pursuant to Article 12 and activities carried out pursuant to Article 35 other than procurement activities, the cost of components originating outside the Union and associated countries shall not be higher than 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the product the increase in production capacity of which is supported by Union funding.

texts.unknown: Give the share of the estimated cost of the components of your end product that originates outside the Union, the EEA EFTA states and Ukraine, and say whether any component originates in Ukraine or in an EEA EFTA state.

rules.note: Article 27(3) applies to procurement and supporting actions, paragraph 4 to industrial reinforcement actions (measured on the product whose production capacity the funding supports). Paragraph 5 also requires that recipients can decide on the design of the products without restrictions imposed by non-associated third countries other than Ukraine; this service does not ask about that. The answer is about one end product.
rules.source_ref: Regulation (EU) 2025/2643, Article 27(3), first sentence, and Article 27(4), first sentence
rules.denominator: the estimated cost of the components of the end product (for industrial reinforcement actions, of the product whose production capacity the funding supports)

passages.text: For procurement carried out pursuant to paragraph 1, points (a) and (c), which is supported by Union funding, the cost of components originating outside the Union and Ukraine shall not be higher than 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product.

For actions carried out pursuant to paragraph 1, point (b), the cost of components originating outside the Union and Ukraine shall not be higher than 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the product the increase in production capacity of which is supported by Union funding.

rules.title: No component from a third country that contravenes the Union's security and defence interests

texts.requires: No component may be sourced from a third country that contravenes the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States.
texts.met: You report no component from a third country that contravenes the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States.
texts.not_met: You report a component from a third country that contravenes the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States. This is an absolute exclusion: the 35 % allowance does not cover it.
texts.unknown: Say whether any component comes from a third country that contravenes the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States. The regulation gives no list of such countries; if you are unsure, ask the contracting authority.

rules.note: This is a separate rule from the 35 % limit. It is a yes or no, with no percentage.
rules.source_ref: Regulation (EU) 2025/2643, Article 27(3), second sentence, and Article 27(4), second sentence

passages.text: No component shall be sourced from third countries that contravene the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States.

No component of the product the increase in production capacity of which is supported by Union funding shall be sourced from third countries that contravene the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States.

rules.title: Subcontractors outside the Union: the 15 to 35 % allowance

texts.info: Common procurement under the Programme can include a subcontractor that is allocated between 15 % and 35 % of the value of the contract and is not established, or has no executive management structures, in the Union or an associated country, if a direct contractual relationship related to the defence product was established between the contractor and that subcontractor before the Regulation entered into force (it was published on 29 December 2025 and entered into force on the following day). This figure is a share of the contract value. It is not the 35 % component cost limit.

rules.note: A 'subcontractor' in the sense of this Regulation is narrower than any supplier: the definition in Article 2 requires at least 15 % of the value of the contract and a need for access to classified information, and leaves out suppliers that deliver components of their own design or production.

passages.text: By way of derogation from paragraph 6, in order to take into account industrial cooperation with non-associated third countries, common procurement that involves a subcontractor that is allocated between 15 % and 35 % of the value of the contract, and that is not established or does not have its executive management structures in the Union or in an associated country, shall be eligible for support under the Programme provided that a direct contractual relationship related to the defence product has been established between the contractor and that subcontractor prior to the date of entry into force of this Regulation.

‘subcontractor’ means an economic operator that is proposed by a candidate, tenderer or contractor to perform specific tasks or services under the supervision of the main contractor, contributing to the design or manufacturing of a defence product, other than what is provided by suppliers to implement the contract, for which it is allocated at least 15 % of the value of the contract, and that needs access to classified information for the performance of that contract; for the purposes of this definition, ‘supplier’ shall be understood as an economic operator that delivers components of its own design or production to the contractor.

rules.title: The action involves Ukraine

texts.info: An action under the Ukraine Support Instrument must be carried out by, or with the involvement of, at a minimum, Ukraine or one legal entity established in Ukraine that also has its executive management structure there. If your company is not established in Ukraine, the action you join needs such a partner.

passages.text: Actions eligible for funding under the Ukraine Support Instrument shall be carried out by, or with the involvement of, at a minimum, Ukraine or one legal entity established and having its executive management structure in Ukraine.

rules.title: Dual-use items moved inside the Union

texts.info: You said you move dual-use items to other EU countries. Such a transfer needs an authorisation only for items listed in Annex IV of Regulation (EU) 2021/821, or where a Member State has imposed one for other dual-use items on the conditions of Article 11(2). Check whether any of your items is in Annex IV and what your Member State has imposed.
texts.not_applicable: This concerns a dual-use product that is moved to other EU countries.

passages.text: An authorisation shall be required for intra-Union transfers of dual-use items listed in Annex IV.

rules.title: Authorisation for military goods

texts.requires: Transfers of defence-related products between Member States are subject to prior authorisation, and Member States' legislation indicates in which cases an export licence is required for military technology and equipment.
texts.met: You hold the authorisation you need for military goods, or have said none is needed.
texts.not_met: You move, or may move, military goods to another EU country, or export them. Transfers between Member States are subject to prior authorisation unless the Member State exempts them, and national law says in which cases an export licence is required. Ask the authority of your Member State.
texts.not_applicable: This concerns military goods that are moved to another EU country or exported. You said your product is not in the military regime, or that you do not export it.

rules.note: Article 4(2) of the Directive lets a Member State exempt some transfers, for example where the supplier or the recipient is a governmental body or part of the armed forces. UNVERIFIED: which authority issues military licences in Germany and Poland. The research notes name the authority for dual-use items only.
rules.source_ref: Directive 2009/43/EC, Article 4(1); Council Common Position 2008/944/CFSP, Article 1(2)

passages.text: The transfer of defence-related products between Member States shall be subject to prior authorisation.

passages.ref: Council Common Position 2008/944/CFSP, Article 1(2), last sentence
passages.text: Member States’ legislation shall indicate in which case an export licence is required with respect to these applications.
